game_concept: A quiz RPG set in Mt. Pyre – Basalt Stair, a basalt column stairway: the forge smith must handle magma slimes while practicing data types & operators. Core idea – Type Sorter: Sort falling obsidian shards into bins labelled int, float, str and bool before they hit the ground.
theme: Mt. Pyre – Basalt Stair: a basalt column stairway
core_gameplay_loop: In Basalt Stair, repeat each round: Sort falling obsidian shards into bins labelled int, float, str and bool before they hit the ground. Each round poses one decision; a wrong answer breaks the streak. Then check the sorted_ok value and advance.
player_objective: Chain 7 consecutive correct decisions about sorted_ok to power up the forge smith and open the ash barrier.
controls: Mouse/touch: drag code blocks into the editor panel; SPACE runs the code; keys 1-4 pick answers.
lose_condition: lives reach 0 (each wrong decision costs a life and resets the streak).
learning_alignment: Week 2 – Data Types & Operators | Level 5 (applied tier): Type Sorter
assets_style: pixel-art volcano: purple-black rock, glowing lava rivers, orange ember light, drifting ash; flat Kenney-style sprites; low war drums, rumbling bass and crackling fire effects
duplicate_check_notes: Unique combination of primary mechanic 'Type Sorter' (Week 2 slot 1), mission type 'Streak Challenge', and setting 'Basalt Stair'. tutorial: Step 1: Look at the code panel. It shows how sorted_ok changes.
Step 2: Use the controls to apply the code idea against magma slimes in Basalt Stair.
Step 3: Win by meeting the goal: streak counter reaches 7.
